title: Trace Sparse Sampler and QuickCard Guide
content:
Purpose
This doc proposes a light-weight, low-cost trace sampling strategy ("sparse sampler") plus a set of compact dashboard QuickCards to speed investigations for tokenized inference requests. Goal: find needles (regressions, cold-cache sessions, multi-model fanouts) with minimal trace volume and dashboard real-estate.

Context and constraints
- We serve tens of millions of inference requests per day; full trace capture is prohibitively expensive for retention and query cost.
- We need deterministic, repeatable heuristics so SREs and oncall can rely on the same signal set.
- Sampling should bias toward operationally meaningful events but remain explainable to customers.

Design principles
- Prioritize signal over volume: capture traces that are most likely to help root-cause latency/errors.
- Keep QuickCards minimal: single-purpose widgets designed for 15–60s triage checks.
- Ensure privacy: redact PII/PHI at capture and apply token-length thresholds before recording raw prompts.

Sparse sampler rules (high level)
1) Always sample 100% of:
   - Inference responses that return 5xx errors from runtime or model-serving layers.
   - Requests with model-selection fallback (automatic downgrade) and canary rollbacks.
   - Requests where output quality monitor flagged a regressions (quality-alert tag).
2) Deterministic rate-limited sampling for everything else, by tenant and route:
   - Base deterministic hash: sha256(tenant_id + route + minute_bucket) -> map to 0..9999.
   - Per-tenant budget default: 5 traces / minute for high-volume tenants, 1 trace / minute for mid, 0.1 trace/min for low. Budgets configurable via feature flags.
3) Heuristic boosters (force a sample if any condition true):
   - latency_p95 > 3x SLO for the route within last 5m
   - tokens_generated > 2048 AND sequence_length_variance > 0.4
   - KV-cache-miss followed by subsequent cold-cache errors in same session window
   - multi-model fanout count >= 3
   - any request exceeding per-token cost threshold (cost spike detector)
4) Adaptive shock mode: when alerting systems detect a service-wide degradation, increase sampling by a factor (x10) for 10 minutes and route traces to a short-lived high-throughput storage bucket for faster query and retention of 48h.

Pseudo-logic (text)
- For each incoming request r:
  - if r.response_code >= 500 or r.quality_alert == true then capture_trace(r, reason="error-or-quality")
  - else if deterministic_hash(r.tenant, r.route, floor(now/minute)) < tenant_budget_threshold(r.tenant) then capture_trace(r, reason="budget")
  - else if any heuristic booster condition true then capture_trace(r, reason="booster")
  - else drop_trace_metadata_only(r) // record small metadata row for global stats and event correlation

What we store per captured trace
- session_id, tenant_id, route, model_version, route_config_id, latency_ms, token_counts (input/out), kv_cache_hit_bool, fanout_count, container/pod id, kernel_hint, node_type, sampling_reason, small redacted prompt snippet (<= 256 chars), trace_start_ts, trace_end_ts
- full prompt only when opt-in and customer consent/enterprise settings permit; default: redacted.

QuickCards: compact dashboard building blocks
- QuickCard intent: a 3–6 metric mini-widget with a clear drill link to linked traces or logs. Designed to be placed in operator consoles and oncall playbooks.
- Each QuickCard includes: title, 1 primary KPI, 2 supporting KPIs, a short explanation line, and a drill link.

Suggested QuickCards for tokenized inference operations
1) Cold-cache heat QuickCard
   - Primary KPI: % of requests with kv_cache_hit == false (5m rolling)
   - Support: p95 latency for cold-cache requests, cold-cache error rate
   - Drill link: filtered traces where kv_cache_hit == false and latency > route_slo * 1.5
   - Use: rapid check for cache warmup regressions after deploys
2) Fanout error spike QuickCard
   - Primary KPI: errors per 10k requests for fanout_count >= 2
   - Support: average fanout_count, model-fallback count
   - Drill: traces showing branch_timeouts and multi-model orchestration spans
3) Token-cost outlier QuickCard
   - Primary KPI: fraction of requests in top 0.5% token cost (24h)
   - Support: median tokens_generated, top-5 tenant ids by cost
   - Drill: sample traces with cost_spike flag
4) Latency ladder QuickCard
   - Primary KPI: p50/p95/p99 latency for route (single compact sparkline)
   - Support: request rate, SLO burn (budget consumed)
   - Drill: grouped traces by latency bucket using sparse sampler reason=booster

Dashboard placement guidelines
- Console default: show 4 QuickCards per route detail page; allow toggling to full dashboard for product/eng investigations.
- Compact operator view: aggregate QuickCards across critical routes into a 2x2 grid for oncall to scan in <30s.
- Full investigation page: include a trace-list panel with sampling_reason filters and small metadata table.

Operational runbook snippets (for oncall)
- First 60s: glance QuickCard grid. If >1 QuickCard shows anomaly, open drill link for the QuickCard with highest severity.
- 2–10 minutes: filter trace-list by sampling_reason in {error-or-quality, booster}. If not enough traces, temporarily enable shock mode via /ops/trace-sampling endpoint.
- 10–60 minutes: correlate with infra metrics (GPU utilization, container restarts, kernel OOMs) and model-change events. Add timeline annotations for deploys and canary rollouts.

Cost and retention model
- Default retained traces: 7 days for sampled traces, 48h for shock-mode extended traces. Keep compact metadata rows for 90 days for billing and capacity planning.
- Storage estimate: at current request volume and default budgets, we project ~1.8M sampled traces / month. With compact storage and aggressive redaction expect ~250GB/month.

Privacy and compliance
- Redaction pipeline runs at capture-time. Remove tokens that match known PII patterns and enforce per-tenant opt-out.
- Enterprise tenants can opt into full-prompt trace capture subject to contract and HSM/KMS requirements.

Migration plan and roll-out steps
1) Build sampler prototype as an Envoy-level filter to ensure deterministic hashing and early budget enforcement (2 sprints).
2) Implement booster rules in runtime telemetry and ensure low-latency signal emission (1 sprint).
3) Create 4 QuickCard widgets in Grafana or console UI and wire drill links to trace-store (1 sprint).
4) Internal beta with eng teams, monitor sampler effectiveness vs previous capture rate for 2 weeks (2 weeks).
5) Roll to prod with gradual per-tenant budget tuning and SLO guardrails.

Measurement and success criteria
- Triaging time reduced: average mean-time-to-insight falls from ~18m to <8m for inferred incidents where traces are relevant.
- Trace capture cost: keep inference-related trace spend under +15% of current telemetry billing while increasing triage utility by >2x.
- False negatives: incidents where no useful trace exists should be <5% of severity>=P2 incidents post-rollout.

Open questions / decisions needed
- Should we treat model-quality regressions reported by Redwood Optimize as an automatic booster? (pros/cons listed in linked Confluence).
- Exact tenant default budgets and whether budgets should be scaled by dollars-spent rather than request volume.
- Where to surface an ops button to temporarily enable shock-mode per-tenant without global impact.

Notes to reviewers
- Look for edge cases where deterministic sampling could bias away from rare but important tenants.
- Security: confirm redaction rules are sufficient for EU privacy regs.
- Implementation detail: prefer a small, testable prototype rather than a full rewrite of current capture pipeline.

Appendix: quick-reference checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Implement deterministic hash and budget enforcement
- [ ] Add booster rule hooks to latency and cost detectors
- [ ] Build Cold-cache and Fanout QuickCards in console
- [ ] Add shock-mode toggle to ops toolkit (audit-logged)
- [ ] Validate redaction and enterprise opt-in flow

End of doc.
